title: MEDI2004 W1 · Introduction to Pharmacology
subject: Pharmacology Fundamentals
content: Drug = any substance producing a biological effect when administered (synthetic, natural, or genetically engineered). Endogenous substances aren't drugs unless administered (own insulin = hormone; injected = drug). Drug = active chemical; medicine = drug + excipients in a dose form (medicine contains the drug); drug class = drugs sharing mechanism/target/therapeutic use. Vitamins/herbs act as drugs when they produce effects (label doesn't decide). Pharmacology = study of drugs and their interactions with living systems; branches: pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, pharmacotherapeutics, toxicology, pharmacogenetics, clinical pharmacology. PK = body->drug (ADME; sets dose/timing); PD = drug->body (mechanism/effect; sets effect & side effects). Classes: analgesic (pain), anaesthetic (removes sensation), anxiolytic (anxiety), sedative (sleep), stimulant (CNS activity), antidepressant (SSRIs), antipsychotic, antihypertensive (ACE inhibitors), antineoplastic (cancer), anabolic steroid, hallucinogen, PrEP (HIV prevention). Prefixes: anti- = against, -lytic = relieves/breaks, an-/anaes- = without.
